stops.date_confidence: attested to 1971 for the physical transfer, supervised by Elizebeth, of the library, papers, the desk from the Capitol Hill house and a small safe, from the Marshall Foundation's own page, fetched in the research pass. William made the arrangement and did not live to see it completed. The incoming pool dated one version of this stop to 1969 and gave two different coordinates, both of them several hundred metres off the foundation's actual location on the VMI post; the coordinate is corrected here and unified. Month and day default.
stops.sun_caveat: year precision: the Sun could be in any sign; the reading above is for the stated (defaulted or conventional) day and should not be trusted
stops.moon_and_planets: omitted: the Moon changes sign every ~2.3 days; only day-precise stops get them

stops.stop: Washington, the patents come out of the vault
stops.date_confidence: attested from USPTO records via Google Patents: US 6,097,812, filed 25 July 1933, issued 1 August 2000; US 6,130,946, from a 1936 application, issued 10 October 2000. The count of nine applications held under secrecy orders is from the dossier. The coordinate is the atlas's canonical Washington point; a patent's issue has no single physical site and none is claimed.

stops.stop: Fort George G. Meade, fifty thousand pages released
stops.date_confidence: attested to 20 April 2015 for the release of about 7,000 records and more than 50,000 pages, roughly 85 percent released in full after line-by-line review, with copies at NARA, on the NSA website and at the Marshall Foundation (US National Archives, 'NSA Declassifies and Releases the Friedman Collection', 30 April 2015). Fort Meade coordinate inherited byte-identical from diffie.journey.json. The quote is Frank Rowlett's foreword to the Six Lectures, written by Friedman's own protege.

stops.stop: Arlington National Cemetery, the stone is read
stops.date_confidence: attested to 17 April 2017, when Elonka Dunin visited the grave and published the solution: the alternating serif and sans-serif letters of KNOWLEDGE IS POWER, read in groups of five as Bacon's biliteral cipher, give WFF. Dunin's page also cites a handwritten note found by Jason Fagone in the Marshall archive in which Elizebeth confirmed the intended plaintext to Ronald Clark, Friedman's 1977 biographer. Dunin is the traveller here in the ordinary sense; the stop is Friedman's because the object is his monument. Coordinate as at the burial stop.
